### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Publisher-wide Elsevier policy (no confirmed Brain Research-specific AI clause; the journal's own Guide for Authors page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and could not be checked). Authors may use generative AI only to improve language/readability pre-submission, with mandatory disclosure via a 'Declaration of Generative AI and AI-assisted technologies' statement above the references (tool name + purpose + extent of human oversight); basic grammar/spell-check is exempt from disclosure. AI cannot generate manuscript text/analysis directly (output may only 'inspire'), cannot create/alter figures or cover art, and cannot be listed as author. Reviewers/editors are separately barred from using generative AI in the evaluation process to protect confidentiality (source: elsevier.com/.../the-use-of-generative-ai-and-ai-assisted-technologies-in-the-review-process). Gate marked conditional: permitted only for disclosed language-polishing, not open use. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/the-use-of-generative-ai-and-ai-assisted-technologies-in-writing-for-elsevier |

- **positioning.methods_welcome (first-hand recent-article sample)**: ScienceDirect blocked direct WebFetch (403) on both the journal homepage and call-for-papers page, so positioning rests on search-engine snippets and general topic tags rather than a first-hand read of actual recent (2024-2026) article titles; confidence capped at signal_quality 2.
